## README.md

Canonical source: [README.md](README.md)

# Wattever

Wattever measures local LLM prefill and decode throughput and GPU power with LM Studio. It records successes and failures across prompt sizes, models and simultaneous query counts, and compares sessions in a browser UI. Use the hosted browser mode with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or the full local helper with Python 3.9+ and LM Studio. Wattever uses the Python standard library and local JavaScript without a package installation or CDN.

## Browser quick start

Open [Wattever on GitHub Pages](https://lpalbou.github.io/Wattever/), start an OpenAI-compatible server, enable its CORS support, and use **Connect** to select models and run tests. Browser and server permissions can affect access to a local endpoint. See [Browser mode](docs/browser.md) for settings, storage, privacy and measurement limits.

## Full local helper quick start

1. Install LM Studio, download the models you want to test, and run `lms bootstrap` once so the `lms` command is available.
2. Get the [v2.4.1 source archive](https://github.com/lpalbou/Wattever/releases/tag/v2.4.1) or clone the repository. The source archive includes historical tracked results.
3. On Windows run `Wattever.bat`; on macOS run `Wattever.command`; on Linux run `sh Wattever.sh`. Alternatively run `python -m wattever.server` from the repository.
4. Open the displayed local URL, select models and workloads on **Run**, and start. Leave the server running until the benchmark finishes. Results appear as cases complete.

See [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md) for setup and [Measurements and sessions](docs/measurements.md) for interpretation and extending a benchmark. GPU monitoring selects a sensor only: configure actual model placement in LM Studio and record GPU setup notes. Power is measured for the selected GPU, not every GPU.

**Results** provides Summary, Table and Compare views with common benchmark, model, measure and concurrency filters. Tables can be copied as tab-separated text. In helper mode, use **Add / rerun tests** to extend a benchmark or replace selected cases. One JSON file stores each benchmark; download it from Results or share it as described in [results guidance](results/README.md). Review its contents before publication.

The hosted Results view also includes a shared catalog that you can browse without connecting a model provider. See [sharing results](docs/sharing-results.md) to contribute your benchmark or add missing tests later.

## Documentation

[Documentation index](docs/README.md) | [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) | [API](docs/api.md) | [FAQ](docs/faq.md) | [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) | [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) | [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) | [Security](SECURITY.md)

Register and use the [Wattever agent skill](https://github.com/lpalbou/Wattever/tree/v2.4.1/skills/wattever) to operate the local API safely. Copy `skills/wattever/` from the version you use into your agent's skills directory.

## docs/getting-started.md

Canonical source: [docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md)

# Getting started

For hosted use without installing Wattever, see [Browser mode](docs/browser.md). The instructions below cover the full local helper.

Install Python 3.9 or newer and [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai/), download the models you want to measure, and run `lms bootstrap` to make the LM Studio CLI available. Wattever does not need Python packages or a JavaScript build. The LM Studio API defaults to `http://localhost:1234`; set `LMS_BASE_URL` before starting Wattever if needed.

Download and extract the [release source archive](https://github.com/lpalbou/Wattever/releases/tag/v2.4.1), or clone the repository. Start `Wattever.bat` on Windows, `Wattever.command` on macOS, or `sh Wattever.sh` on Linux. You can also run `python -m wattever.server` in the repository. The server listens on loopback and prints its URL; keep its window open. `GPU_BENCH_PORT` sets the starting port (default 8713); `GPU_BENCH_NO_BROWSER=1` suppresses automatic browser opening.

On **Run**, select installed models, prompt sizes, query counts and settings. Choose a GPU sensor and, for multiple GPUs, describe the LM Studio placement in GPU setup notes. Start the benchmark and view live results. Model loads and inference can take substantial time and change LM Studio's loaded models. The macOS launcher offers optional administrator authorization for `powermetrics`; speed measurements still work without it.

Use **Results** to select and compare benchmark files, download JSON, or copy tables. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md) before comparing and [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) if setup fails. Return to [overview](README.md); see [API](docs/api.md) for integration.

---

## docs/browser.md

Canonical source: [docs/browser.md](docs/browser.md)

# Browser mode

Open [Wattever on GitHub Pages](https://lpalbou.github.io/Wattever/) to run a quick benchmark without installing Wattever. Start LM Studio or another OpenAI-compatible server with models available. Enter its endpoint (the default is `http://localhost:1234/v1`) and select **Connect**; Wattever does not request the model list until you connect. Choose models and workloads, start the benchmark, and keep the page open until it finishes.

The provider must permit cross-origin requests. LM Studio has an Enable CORS switch in its [server settings](https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/core/server/settings). Browsers may also require local-network permission, and HTTPS-to-localhost behavior depends on the browser and its security settings; see [Microsoft Edge local network access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/ms-edge-local-network-access). Wattever connects directly from the browser: it has no hosted proxy and does not use helper credentials. If the endpoint needs an API key, enter it in the page; the key stays in memory and the input clears after connecting. It is not saved in result files or browser storage.

Chrome versions with separate network permissions may call localhost access **Apps on device** or **Loopback network**. Allow the permission for the Wattever site when you connect. The permission is distinct from access to other devices on your LAN; see [Chrome local network guidance](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance/blob/main/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/security/local-network-access.md).

GPU, CPU, RAM and VRAM fields are optional user-supplied descriptions, not hardware discovery. Browser mode cannot measure GPU power or VRAM use, load or unload models, choose model placement, allocate context, control MTP or reasoning, resume a session, or add and rerun cases in the same file. The provider manages those settings; configure it separately. Use the [full local helper](docs/getting-started.md) when those controls and telemetry are needed.

Browser results record `measurement_mode: browser`, `browser_schema_version: 1` and protocol `browser-1`, with the bundled corpus identity and a SHA-256 hash when available. Timing occurs in the client; it includes network and browser overhead and is not directly comparable to helper protocol measurements. Prompt throughput is unavailable when the provider does not report exact prompt usage. Output token counts and throughput are marked estimated when completion usage is unavailable. A failed request is recorded as a failure, not zero throughput.

Results are stored in browser storage and can be downloaded or imported as JSON. Storage can be cleared or unavailable; if a storage warning appears, download the in-memory results before closing the page. Closing or reloading the page stops the browser benchmark, and a previously running result is shown as interrupted. On timeout the browser aborts its requests and stops the run, but cannot verify that the provider stopped inference or unload its model. Check the provider before starting another workload. Helper benchmarks instead continue in the local server when the page closes; see [measurements and sessions](docs/measurements.md).

Results also shows a read-only shared catalog without requiring an endpoint connection. Hiding a shared result affects only this browser. See [sharing results](docs/sharing-results.md) to contribute a benchmark.

## Shared-results data boundary

The hosted site opens the shared Results library by default. Browsing it reads only the same-origin GitHub Pages catalog and benchmark JSON; it does not query desktop helper APIs or local files. Shared records identify their GitHub source. The published JSON omits host-local diagnostic text and paths while preserving measurements, failure classifications, hardware descriptions, settings and session provenance. It is a public projection of the repository record.

If the browser data client fails to load, the hosted site reports that failure rather than falling back to desktop APIs. Model-server access belongs to the optional Run workflow and starts only after an explicit Connect action.

---

## docs/sharing-results.md

Canonical source: [docs/sharing-results.md](docs/sharing-results.md)

# Sharing and continuing benchmark results

The hosted Results view includes a shared catalog built from benchmark JSON files in this repository, alongside results stored in your browser. You can browse shared results without connecting a model provider or entering an API key. Shared entries are read-only; deleting one in the hosted view hides it in that browser and does not delete it from GitHub. Local browser results can be renamed and deleted locally.

## Contribute a benchmark

1. Run a benchmark using the [full helper](docs/getting-started.md) or [browser mode](docs/browser.md). Partial sessions and failures are useful contributions too.
2. In Results, download the benchmark's **JSON**. Review the hardware information, notes and model names before sharing. Browser results identify their separate client-timed protocol; helper results include the sensor and session settings.
3. Sign in to GitHub and open [upload files to results/runs](https://github.com/lpalbou/Wattever/upload/main/results/runs). Upload the single JSON file, named after its `id` with a `.json` extension. If you do not have write access, follow GitHub's fork prompt and propose the change from your fork.
4. Open the proposed pull request. The repository's validation checks run on the contribution. Once merged and the site deployment completes, the shared catalog updates automatically.

For a command-line contribution, fork and clone the repository, create a branch, and copy the single result file to `results/runs/`. Run `python tools/validate_results.py results/runs/<id>.json`, then `git add results/runs/<id>.json`, commit, push your branch and open a pull request. Stage the specific result file so unrelated local files and deletions are excluded.

## Add missing tests later

A benchmark does not need every planned case before you contribute it. To complete or extend a helper benchmark later, download its JSON and put it in the local helper's `results/runs/` directory using its `id` as the filename. In Results select it and choose **Add / rerun tests**. Existing models are preselected; select the models, sizes and query counts you want, review the preview, and choose **Add missing tests**. Existing terminal cases are preserved. Select **Retry failed tests** explicitly if you also want to retry failures and skipped cases.

The helper checks hardware, selected GPU and driver, corpus and LM Studio version for compatibility. Start a separate benchmark when those differ or cannot be verified. The same file records the added session and the helper saves a backup before modifying it. To update a contribution, submit the updated file with the same ID in a pull request; the saved cases travel with it. Do not manually edit measurements or replace failures with zeroes.

Browser mode can import and display JSON but cannot continue an existing benchmark. Its provider controls model execution and context. See [measurements and sessions](docs/measurements.md) for retry, replacement and comparison rules.

---

## docs/measurements.md

Canonical source: [docs/measurements.md](docs/measurements.md)

# Measurements and sessions

The details below describe the full local helper. Browser mode has a separate `browser-1` protocol and client-side timings; its measurements are not directly comparable with helper measurements. See [Browser mode](docs/browser.md).

A case combines a model, Standard or MTP mode, prompt size, simultaneous query count and repeat. The runner records successful, failed and skipped cases; inability to load or fit a workload is useful capacity information. MTP requires a model with a supported bundled MTP head. Reasoning is disabled by default; settings and runtime versions accompany results.

Prefill throughput is prompt tokens divided by time to first token (TTFT), including overhead before the first token. Decode throughput is (completion tokens minus the first token) divided by the time from the first token to completion. Output token counts may be estimated when exact usage is unavailable. Group throughput for concurrent requests includes prefill and queueing and is distinct from per-request decode speed. Compare matching model builds, settings, corpus and protocol, and interpret differences in runtime placement and memory conditions.

The default per-test context allocation reserves prompt tokens, output budget, 512 tokens of headroom and a 5% prompt safety margin, subject to the model's per-request maximum. The shared KV allocation is the per-request capacity multiplied by simultaneous queries. Workloads are grouped by model. The default per-test policy reloads for each context and concurrency allocation; the optional fixed policy uses the largest planned allocation for a model and MTP mode, reducing reloads while changing memory conditions. More concurrency consumes more memory; large contexts can fail to fit.

NVIDIA telemetry uses `nvidia-smi` for the selected card's board power. macOS may use `powermetrics` for GPU and CPU rails with permission. These measure different boundaries; whole-system power is estimated, not a meter reading, and includes only the selected GPU sensor. GPU sensor selection does not direct LM Studio placement. Record placement separately. Missing sensor data remains unavailable. Hardware inventory is best effort and lists discoverable GPUs, CPU, memory and other equipment without serial numbers or unique IDs.

Each new benchmark has one JSON file in `results/runs/`. **Add / rerun tests** on an existing benchmark can select models and their Standard/MTP modes, prompt sizes and query counts. Choose an action and review the case counts in the preview: the default adds missing cases; retry failed also retries skipped cases; rerun selected tests replaces selected cases including successful ones. A replaced attempt is archived in `previous_attempts`, not averaged or included in a median with its replacement. Before changing the file, an exact snapshot is kept under `results/.history/`. Each execution records its own session settings and provenance. Resume creates a new run for unfinished work. Extension and resume require compatible hardware, selected GPU and driver, corpus and LM Studio version; when compatibility cannot be verified, start a new benchmark.

The helper's request deadline uses successful same-model prefill throughput when available: six times projected prefill time plus 120 seconds, capped by the configured test timeout. Without a comparable result it uses the configured timeout. After the first token, 120 seconds without output progress also triggers recovery (or the configured timeout if shorter). These are time limits, not detection of a physical freeze or GPU-memory threshold. A timeout is recorded; the helper verifies model unload and request workers exit before continuing. If verification fails, the run stops for manual recovery. With the default skip setting, larger cases for that model and concurrency are skipped after failure.

Prompt presets are 512, 5k, 10k, 20k, 40k, 80k, 100k, 120k, 150k, 200k and 260k tokens; concurrency presets are 1 through 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 50, 75 and 100 simultaneous queries. Compare cases at matching dimensions.

Older schemas and planner settings remain readable. Extending a legacy benchmark can produce sessions with different context planning; compare session settings rather than treating them as identical. See [API](docs/api.md), [FAQ](docs/faq.md), and [results guidance](results/README.md).

The Add / rerun tests dialog preselects installed benchmark models and their saved techniques. New models are unchecked; unavailable benchmark models remain visible. Per-model successful, failed, skipped and unfinished counts cover saved techniques and selected additions at the displayed prompt sizes and query counts. Changing or clearing this selection leaves recorded measurements intact. The preview shows which cases the chosen action will execute.

---

## docs/architecture.md

Canonical source: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)

# Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    UI[Local browser UI] -->|HTTP on loopback| Server[Wattever server]
    Server --> Runner[Benchmark runner]
    Runner -->|CLI and streaming API| LMS[LM Studio]
    Runner --> Corpus[Local prompt corpus]
    Runner --> Sensors[GPU and system telemetry]
    Runner --> Store[JSON results and history]
    Server --> Store
    Server --> UI
    Hosted[Hosted browser UI] --> Adapter[Browser adapter]
    Adapter -->|OpenAI-compatible API| Provider[Model provider]
    Adapter --> BrowserStore[Browser storage and JSON export]
```

The standard-library server serves local static assets and coordinates one benchmark at a time. The runner plans cases, loads models through LM Studio, collects streaming responses and optional power samples, and saves progress to JSON. The UI reads status and events and displays saved results. System discovery and sensor access are platform dependent; no external service is required by Wattever itself. The LM Studio endpoint can be configured separately.

The selected sensor and model execution placement are separate. Result files preserve case and session provenance; power estimates have a different boundary from GPU measurements. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md), [API](docs/api.md), and [getting started](docs/getting-started.md).

The hosted browser adapter connects directly to the configured provider after the user chooses Connect. It has no hosted proxy or helper credentials and cannot access helper telemetry or control model loading. The browser and helper use different measurement protocols; see [browser mode](docs/browser.md).

---

## docs/api.md

Canonical source: [docs/api.md](docs/api.md)

# Local HTTP API

This reference describes the full local helper. Hosted [browser mode](docs/browser.md) uses an in-page adapter, not this HTTP service, and does not support extensions, resume, model unload or telemetry.

The server binds to `127.0.0.1` on port 8713 by default, or the next available port. Set `GPU_BENCH_PORT` to change the starting port. This local interface is intended for a trusted local user, not exposure to a network. JSON errors have an `error` field; invalid input and runtime conflicts generally return 400, missing runs 404, active-run metadata edits or deletion 409, and unexpected failures 500.

Read endpoints: `GET /api/version`, `/api/env`, `/api/models`, `/api/status`, `/api/events?cursor=0`, `/api/runs`, `/api/runs/<id>`, `/api/runs/<id>/download`, `/api/preview?tokens=512`, `/api/export.json` and `/api/export.csv`. Exports accept comma-separated `ids`; without them they include all runs. `GET /api/bench/extend-plan?run_id=<id>` supplies extension options.

State-changing endpoints: `POST /api/bench/start` accepts benchmark configuration; `/api/bench/cancel` requests cancellation; `/api/bench/resume` accepts `run_id`; `/api/bench/extend-plan` previews a selection; `/api/bench/extend` starts it. Extension selection includes `run_id`, `model_modes` (model IDs mapped to arrays of `off` and/or `on`), `sizes`, `concurrency_levels`, `retry_failed`, and `rerun_existing`. Defaults add missing cases; `retry_failed` includes failed and skipped cases; `rerun_existing` includes successful selected cases. Plan first and review its counts. Starting, resuming or extending loads and unloads models, performs inference and writes results; extension saves a history snapshot.

`POST /api/lmstudio/start` starts the LM Studio server, `/api/lmstudio/unload` unloads models, `POST /api/runs/<id>/meta` changes label and notes, `DELETE /api/runs/<id>` moves a run to local trash, and `POST /api/shutdown` stops Wattever. These calls change local state. The active run cannot be edited or deleted. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md) for compatibility and [architecture](docs/architecture.md) for the system boundary.

## Configuration and examples

`LMS_BASE_URL` selects the LM Studio API (default `http://localhost:1234`). `GPU_BENCH_PORT` selects the starting local port and `GPU_BENCH_NO_BROWSER=1` suppresses the browser. A new benchmark accepts a JSON object such as:

```json
{"models":["<installed-model-id>"],"sizes":[512,5000],"concurrency_levels":[1,2],"max_tokens":256,"repeats":1}
```

Send it to `POST /api/bench/start` only when ready to run inference. Omitted configuration uses these defaults:

| Setting | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `sizes` | 512, 5000, 10000, 20000, 40000 |
| `concurrency_levels`, `repeats`, `max_tokens` | `[1]`, 1, 256 |
| `gpu_offload`, `fallback_on_failure`, `stop_model_after_failure` | `max`, true, true |
| `context_policy`, `context_headroom`, `context_safety_fraction` | `per_test`, 512, 0.05 |
| `mtp_modes`, `warmup`, `disable_thinking` | `["off"]`, true, true |
| `load_timeout_s`, `per_test_timeout_s`, `power_interval_ms` | 900, 1800, 150 |
| `gpu_index` | 0 (telemetry sensor only) |

For `POST /api/bench/extend-plan`, use a selection like:

```json
{"run_id":"<run-id>","model_modes":{"<installed-model-id>":["off","on"]},"sizes":[512,5000],"concurrency_levels":[1,2],"retry_failed":false,"rerun_existing":false}
```

Review the returned counts and warnings before submitting the selection to `/api/bench/extend`. **Add / rerun tests** modifies the existing benchmark after taking a snapshot; `/api/bench/resume` instead creates a separate run with unfinished work and a link to its source. Compatibility checks apply to both; see [measurements](docs/measurements.md).

---

## docs/faq.md

Canonical source: [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md)

# FAQ

## Can I run without installing Wattever?

Yes. The hosted [browser mode](docs/browser.md) connects directly to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The endpoint and browser must allow the connection; telemetry, model control and same-file extensions require the full helper.

## Does the selected GPU determine where inference runs?

No. It selects a telemetry sensor. Configure LM Studio placement separately and record the setup in notes. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md).

## Are power numbers comparable?

GPU board and SoC rail measurements have different boundaries; estimated whole-system power is not a wall meter and only includes the selected GPU. Compare like sources and settings.

## Can I compare old and new files?

Older files remain readable. Compare protocol, model, corpus, settings, context planner and session provenance; legacy and newer context allocation can differ within an extended benchmark. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md).

## Does a failed case invalidate the benchmark?

No. Failures and skipped cases are recorded and can be retried. See [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) for common causes.

## Must a benchmark be complete before I share it?

No. Partial sessions are useful contributions. The helper can add missing cases to the same file later, subject to its compatibility checks. See [sharing results](docs/sharing-results.md).

---

## docs/troubleshooting.md

Canonical source: [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md)

# Troubleshooting

- **Hosted page cannot connect:** check the endpoint URL, server availability, CORS and your browser's local-network permission. HTTPS-to-localhost behavior varies by browser. See [browser mode](docs/browser.md).
- **Browser storage warning:** download the result JSON before closing the page; an in-memory result is lost on reload.
- **Helper timeout recovery stopped:** inspect LM Studio and ensure the model and requests have stopped before starting another run. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md).

- **LM Studio or models unavailable:** install LM Studio, run `lms bootstrap`, start its server and check that the models are downloaded. Verify `LMS_BASE_URL` if using a different endpoint. Reopen Wattever and check the Run page.
- **Power unavailable:** check `nvidia-smi` for NVIDIA sensors. On macOS, use the launcher and accept the optional power prompt; without authorization speed tests still work. Other sensors may not provide power. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md).
- **Load failure or context overflow:** reduce prompt size or simultaneous queries, inspect model context limits and available memory, or choose a smaller model. A failure is retained in results; use the retry option after correcting the cause.
- **Extension rejected:** hardware, selected GPU and driver, corpus and LM Studio version must match. Start a separate benchmark if they changed or cannot be verified. See [sessions](docs/measurements.md).
- **No response from Wattever:** check the URL printed by its launcher and keep the server window open. The default starting port is 8713 but another available port may be selected. See [getting started](docs/getting-started.md).

- **File-save warning:** update and restart the desktop helper, then use **Add / rerun tests ? Add missing tests** to continue. Completed records remain saved. The warning?s **Technical details** disclosure contains the original diagnostic.

---

## CONTRIBUTING.md

Canonical source: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)

# Contributing

Share benchmark results by opening a pull request with one JSON file in `results/runs/`. The [sharing guide](docs/sharing-results.md) explains the GitHub upload workflow and how to add missing tests later. Review the file for information you do not want to publish and follow [results guidance](results/README.md). Record model builds, placement and relevant settings so readers can interpret results.

For code changes, preserve old result readability, distinguish measured values from estimates, and document changes in measurement semantics. Wattever uses the Python standard library and local browser assets. See [architecture](docs/architecture.md), [API](docs/api.md), [changelog](CHANGELOG.md), and [security](SECURITY.md).

Run the software checks applicable to your change:

```sh
python -m unittest discover -s tests
node --check web/app.js
node tests/test_ui.js
node tests/test_tables.js
python tools/validate_results.py
```

The optional browser test is `node tests/test_ui_browser.cjs`. State which platforms and real hardware you exercised; software tests cannot establish GPU performance. Follow the [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

---

## SECURITY.md

Canonical source: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)

# Security

Wattever serves a local interface that can start benchmarks, load or unload models, and change local results. Keep it bound to loopback and use it only on a trusted machine. Review result files before sharing them.

Report suspected vulnerabilities privately to the repository maintainers through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting if available. Do not publish sensitive details before maintainers can respond. See [API](docs/api.md) for state-changing endpoints.

---

## CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

Canonical source: [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

# Code of conduct

Treat participants with respect. Be constructive, welcome differing experience levels, and avoid harassment, discrimination and personal attacks. Maintainers may remove inappropriate contributions or limit participation to protect the community. Report concerns privately to the repository maintainers through GitHub. See [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## CHANGELOG.md

Canonical source: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)

# Changelog

## Unreleased

- Keeps shared Results on GitHub-hosted catalog data, omits local execution diagnostics from public exports, and fails closed if the hosted data client is unavailable.

- Shows readable benchmark-save errors with optional technical details and refreshes shared data consistently after updates.

- Retains the latest RTX 5060 Ti session in the shared results library; removes older runs and preliminary snapshots.

- Adds a shared results catalog to the hosted Results view and a guide for contributing and continuing benchmark files.

## 2.4.1 - 2026-10-27

- Keeps viewport position and keyboard focus stable when toggling measures in Summary, Table and Compare.
- Includes a labelled preliminary RTX 5060 Ti result snapshot with its incompleteness and measurement limitations recorded.

- Preselects existing benchmark models when adding tests and shows each model's successful, failed, skipped and unfinished cases. New and unavailable models are distinguished; saved measurements remain intact when changing the selection.

## 2.4.0 - 2026-10-27

- Introduces measurement protocol 2, cross-platform hardware inventory, Linux support, concurrent queries and per-session provenance.
- Stores a benchmark in one JSON file and adds live case results, shared Results filters, chart comparisons and copyable tables.
- Adds same-file extensions, failed and skipped retries, selected-case reruns, attempt history and snapshots. Successful replacements remain separate from archived attempts.
- Plans shared KV capacity per concurrent request with a 5% prompt margin and supports a fixed context policy. Standard and MTP modes can be chosen per model.
- Adds hosted browser mode with direct OpenAI-compatible connections, local import/export and a separate measurement protocol.
- Adds adaptive request deadlines and verified model unload and worker recovery before continuing after a timeout.
- Adds a documentation set and an agent skill for the local API.
- Older concurrent failures may reflect legacy context allocation rather than a model capacity limit; use the session planner information when interpreting them.
- Older result schemas and planner settings remain readable. Extended files may contain sessions using different planners; compare provenance and settings before combining measurements.

## 1.0.0

- Initial release.

## results/README.md

Canonical source: [results/README.md](results/README.md)

# Benchmark sessions

One benchmark is one JSON file in `runs/`. A session contains every model,
prompt size, concurrency level, repeat and failure measured for one machine
configuration. Changing cards or runtime GPU placement means starting a new
session. Historical unversioned files remain readable without rewriting them.

## Run and contribute

1. Launch Wattever and click **Reset for all models** to select every downloaded
   language model and restore the standard measurement settings.
2. Give the session a useful label, such as `RTX 5060 Ti - stock`. Choose prompt
   sizes and concurrent request counts. Default concurrency is one; click **10**
   to select all levels from one through ten. Prompt-length badges work the same way. Review the total request count.
3. With multiple cards, configure placement in LM Studio and describe it in the
   **Runtime GPU placement** field. The sensor selector controls power readings
   only. It does not change where LM Studio executes the model.
4. Run the benchmark. Failures and partial sessions remain useful data.
5. Download **JSON** in Results, or take the matching file from `results/runs/`.
   Review it for details you do not want to publish.
6. Follow the [sharing guide](docs/sharing-results.md) to upload the file and
   propose a pull request. Validation runs on the contribution and the shared
   catalog updates after merge. No index or aggregate file changes are needed.

## Standard format

New files use `schema_version: 2`. See [benchmark.schema.json](results/benchmark.schema.json).
Fields are additive; the existing `gpu`, `host`, `config` and `results` fields remain.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `application` | Tool version and measurement protocol version |
| `hardware.os` | OS name, release and architecture |
| `hardware.cpu` | CPU name, physical and logical core counts |
| `hardware.system` | Manufacturer/model and physical RAM in bytes |
| `hardware.gpus` | Separate entries for every discoverable adapter; name, vendor, memory in bytes, driver and optional sensor index |
| `hardware.motherboard`, `hardware.firmware`, `hardware.storage` | Best-effort board model, firmware vendor/version and physical disk models/capacity/interface |
| `classification` | Hardware configuration grouping hash, GPU names and platform; not a unique machine identity |
| `measurement_scope` | Which GPU sensor supplies power and user-reported runtime placement |
| `corpus.sha256` | Corpus fingerprint for comparing the exact workload |
| `config` | Selected models, prompt targets, concurrency levels and measurement settings |
| `results` | Measurements, failures, skips and cancellation records |

Unknown metadata is `null` or an empty collection. Hardware discovery is best
effort; an empty adapter list does not prove that the machine has no GPU.
New files omit GPU UUIDs, serial numbers, usernames and hostnames. User-entered
notes and runtime/model names are included; review them before sharing. Historical
files may still contain a GPU UUID; it may be removed without changing measurements.

## Concurrent measurements

Each result row includes `concurrency`; missing means one in historical files.
Single-request prefill/decode retain their original definitions. Groups above
one contain `requests`, including per-request status, TTFT and decode speed.
Each concurrent request has its own leading nonce to invalidate prefix caching.
`lms load --parallel` sets the runtime's prediction capacity for that level.

`aggregate_completion_tps` is successful requests' total output tokens divided
by group wall time, including prefill and queueing. It is not the sum of individual
decode speeds. A group is successful only when every request succeeds. If usage
counts are unavailable, stream chunks supply an estimate and the result says so.
The UI marks estimated token counts and derived throughput with `*`.

`group_power` covers the group interval. Concurrent phases overlap, so they do
not get invented prefill/decode energy splits. Power is for the selected GPU
sensor, never the sum of all connected cards. Whole-system power remains an
estimate and omits other GPUs' load; do not treat it as a wall-meter measurement.
Compare equivalent model/quantization, context, concurrency, offload, reasoning,
MTP, output budget, protocol and corpus before attributing differences to hardware.

## Local cleanup

**Results -> Delete** removes that session from the local application and
moves its JSON into ignored `results/.trash/`. Active runs must stop first. To
restore a session, move its archived JSON back into `results/runs/` and rename it
to the `id` inside the file plus `.json`, then refresh Results.

Deleting a tracked result produces a local Git deletion. This does not remove
the upstream copy; include only your new session file in a result contribution.

## Add, continue or rerun tests

In Results, select a benchmark and choose **Add / rerun tests**. Select models and
their Standard/MTP techniques, prompt sizes and query counts. Choose an action:

- **Add missing tests** runs cases without a completed result.
- **Retry failed tests** includes failed and skipped cases as well as missing ones.
- **Rerun selected tests** includes successful cases too. Select one model to
  replace its measurements, or use **Select benchmark models** to select the
  installed models and techniques from the benchmark.

The preview separates new cases, failed retries, successful reruns and existing
measurements. Replacement is explicit; existing successful cases are preserved
when adding or retrying. Measurements use the same `results/runs/<id>.json` file.
Before execution, an exact local backup is written under ignored
`results/.history/`. Replaced rows move into `previous_attempts` with their
original session identifier, archive time and reason. Charts and summary medians
use active results, so replacements are not averaged with archived attempts.

`config` describes the benchmark's combined selections. Each item in `sessions`
records the settings used by that execution; result `session_id` links back to
it. `execution_config` is the most recent workload selection. This provenance
matters when extending an older planner run or adding MTP for one model.
`remaining_tests` counts requested cases with no terminal result.

Partial and completed benchmarks can both be shared. To add missing tests later,
use the same file and follow [sharing results](docs/sharing-results.md).
